items.note: The page bounds $m^{1-2^{-50}}=m\exp(-2^{-50}\log m)>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta)$ using $\log m<20$ and compares with $s/W=m(1-\eta)$, exactly the paper's route (lines 1319-1346); it also places the result in the recurrence $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$ to show why $s/W<m^\tau$ gives $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

The page gives the definition $\eta=(Wm-s)/(Wm)$, the two exact values and the claim 'both greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$', but does not compute them from $s,W$ (or $L_{\rm b},L_{\rm c}$) and does not carry out the comparison (e.g. $\eta_{\rm c}\approx3.7\cdot10^{-12}$ against $20\cdot2^{-50}\approx1.8\cdot10^{-14}$). This matches the paper's own level of detail; nothing is wrong.
'Since $m<2^{20}$ and $\log 2<1$, we have $\log m<20$' gives the reason, as the paper does. The page does not recall $m=10^6$, which is what makes $m<2^{20}$ true, but the passage does not need it.

The chain $m\exp(-2^{-50}\log m)>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta)$ is shown, with the justification '$e^{-x}>1-x$ for $x>0$' added. The last step relies on S4.4.1's $\eta>20\cdot2^{-50}$, as in the paper.

The page uses 'Since $s/W=m(1-\eta)$', which is correct from the definition of $\eta$, to conclude $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$, $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $0<\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}<1$, matching the paper.

errors.quote: Replace each scalar by an array of logical volume $V$, the total size of the array, and use [Elementary stream operations](elementary-stream-ops.md) to split it into $W$ role streams of volume $V/W$.
errors.problem: Read literally, each of the $W$ wires carries an array of volume $V$, which would make the total $WV$. In the paper (lines 1497-1502), the single input array of logical volume $V$ is split by rows into $W$ role streams. Each wire then carries one role stream of volume $V/W$.
The page has already named the recursion parameter $e=m^k$ (and writes $F_k=O(e^\tau)$). Using $e$ here for Euler's number clashes with that. The paper avoids the clash by writing $\exp(\cdot)$.
